item.title: Steady growth trajectory driven by innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
October's economic data point to a steadily improving Chinese economy that is undergoing structural upgrading despite global uncertainties. In particular, double-digit growth in high-tech manufacturing and a surge in investment in intellectual property products highlight the resilience and vibrancy of the world's second-largest economy. The Chinese economy grew 4.6 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters, with the October data suggesting this steady trajectory remains intact. The essence of the country's economic strength lies in the shift from traditional growth drivers to new and innovative engines. Last month, the value added of high-tech manufacturing rose by 17.6 percent year-on-year, picking up pace from September and reflecting the rapid industrial upgrading underway across the country. In a breakdown, the production of 3D-printing equipment, lithium-ion batteries and industrial robots surged by 85.9 percent, 30 percent and 26 percent year-on-year, respectively, while the output of new energy vehicles increased by 17.1 percent. As traditional factor-driven expansion gives way to technology-led and advanced manufacturing growth, it enables the country's economy to better withstand external shocks and internal pressures, laying a solid foundation for long-term sustainable growth. Wang Guanhua, a spokesman for the National Bureau of Statistics, noted on Monday that the transition from traditional to new growth drivers is the result of the country's persistent efforts over many years to promote high-quality development, which will provide stronger support for the economy going forward. Moreover, increasing investment in intellectual property products — up by 9.2 percent in the first 10 months of the year compared with the same period last year — suggests that companies are prioritizing innovation and future productivity through R&D, software and databases rather than physical assets. Its share of total investment rose by 2.5 percentage points year-on-year, effectively promoting scientific and technological innovation. As market resources continuously flow into research and technological breakthroughs, innovation is becoming a systematic driving force that boosts industrial upgrading. It is releasing China's economic vitality and fueling high-quality development. From a foreign trade perspective, as global demand for smart and green goods expands, China's high-tech and green products have shown strong growth momentum. In October, exports of both high-tech products and the "new three" products — namely photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles — all increased by more than 50 percent year-on-year. Additionally, strong import growth has become further evidence of the sizable domestic demand. China's imports surged by 23.6 percent in the first 10 months of the year, with October alone witnessing a year-on-year increase of 34.7 percent. The upgrading of consumption demand and industrial modernization have boosted the demand for quality goods, advanced equipment and technological products from global markets. Against the backdrop of sluggish global growth and complex external challenges, China's expanding imports deliver tangible opportunities that can help propel a global recovery, positioning the country as a key stabilizer of the world economy. Factors that previously dragged on the economy are also showing signs of improvement. For instance, the inventory of newly built commercial housing has continued to shrink, thanks mainly to supportive government measures. By the end of October, the floor area of unsold newly built commercial housing had decreased by 1.7 percent year-on-year, a decline 0.2 percentage points larger than at the end of September, marking eight consecutive months of decline. The government will continue to manage new housing supply and reduce inventory to ensure the healthy development of the market. The long-term positive fundamentals of China's economy remain unchanged. With continuous structural reform, strengthened innovation capacity and expanding domestic market momentum, China is on track to meet its full-year growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent. This will also inject strong vitality into global growth.

item.title: Shenzhou XXIV to launch soon with first Chinese-foreign astronaut team
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
China's next manned mission, the Shenzhou XXIV, is scheduled to be launched in the near future to transport three astronauts to the Tiangong space station, according to the China Manned Space Agency. The Shenzhou XXIV crew spacecraft and its carrier, a Long March 2F rocket, were moved to the service tower on Tuesday at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China's Gobi Desert, the agency said in a brief news release, adding that launch facilities at the spaceport "are in good condition." The release noted that the Shenzhou XXIV spacecraft and the rocket will undergo final functional checks in the next several days, and the launch will take place in due course. The upcoming mission is set to mark the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program, as a Pakistani astronaut has been selected to work as the payload specialist in the Shenzhou XXIV crew and spend a multi-day journey inside the Tiangong, before returning to Earth with two Chinese astronauts from the Shenzhou XXIII team.

item.title: Shenzhen welcomes foreign officials for key meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo arrived in Shenzhen, in South China's Guangdong province, on Monday, marking the start of a series of arrivals by leaders of the economies for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. This is Sheinbaum's first trip to China since assuming office in 2024, with four cabinet ministers accompanying her. Sheinbaum is also scheduled to hold talks with President Xi Jinping during her stay in the city, focusing on technology, renewable energy, environmental cooperation, and scientific development. It is reported that the objectives of her visit are to deepen economic, trade and industrial cooperation with China and lay the groundwork for hosting APEC meetings in 2028. Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also arrived in Shenzhen on Monday. More leaders from APEC economies are expected to arrive in the following days ahead of the meeting. Wang Junsheng, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' National Institute of International Strategy, said that the enthusiasm among APEC member economies for this year's meeting reflects a shared desire for development and closer regional cooperation, particularly at a time of mounting economic uncertainty and rising trade protectionism. Economic ties among the 21 APEC members are deeply intertwined, Wang said, with China serving as the largest trading partner for 13 of them. In the first three quarters of 2026, eight of China's top 10 trading partners were APEC economies. Given that the Asia-Pacific accounts for more than 60 percent of global GDP, closer economic cooperation and regional integration are crucial not only to the development of individual economies but also to regional and global prosperity, Wang said. China has long been a strong advocate and active practitioner of openness and cooperation, Wang noted. Restrictions removed In November 2024, China removed all market access restrictions on foreign investment in the manufacturing sector, further opening its market and promoting deeper integration between domestic and international markets. The move has created greater opportunities for foreign businesses to invest in China, expand cooperation and benefit from the country's development, Wang said. The strong interest in this year's meeting also reflects high expectations for China as the host economy, Wang said, adding that many APEC members are looking to China to play a greater role in promoting free trade, advancing regional economic integration and creating new opportunities for shared growth. zhoujin@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Chinese, Russian, US heads of state to hold landmark talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump will meet in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province, on Thursday for the first-ever face-to-face summit of the three countries' heads of state, a groundbreaking gathering that experts said could boost global stability, dialogue and cooperation. Speaking at a regular news briefing on Monday, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the three leaders will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations. China, Russia and the United States are all founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of the UN Security Council, Mao noted, adding that in history, the three countries fought side by side to secure victory in the World Anti-Fascist War. Under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder important responsibilities to work together to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability, she said. Strengthening communication, managing differences and stabilizing relations serve the interests of all three countries and meet the expectations of the international community, Mao added, saying that such efforts would help stabilize the global situation and advance dialogue and cooperation. The trilateral summit could send a strong political signal of stability in major-country relations, bolstering international confidence in the prospects for global development, experts said. Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said that the summit will demonstrate again the irreplaceable role of head-of-state diplomacy in providing strategic guidance. Wang said China does not subscribe to the logic that the world can be run by major countries, but advocates stronger coordination and cooperation among them. In seeking to reform and improve global governance and build a community with a shared future for humanity, China champions an equal and orderly multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations, he added. Konstantin Kosachev, deputy speaker of Russia's Federation Council, said the trilateral summit would carry significant symbolic weight, reflecting recognition of a multipolar world in which no single power can address all global challenges alone. In an interview published by Russia's weekly newspaper Argumenty i Fakty on Saturday, he cautioned against describing the summit as a "new Yalta" — a reference to a major conference in 1945 of the leaders of the United States, the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union — saying he expected discussions to focus on coordinating interests and preventing confrontation rather than dividing the world into spheres of influence. Gao Fei, president of China Foreign Affairs University, said China's comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for a new era with Russia and its efforts to stabilize ties with the US helped create favorable conditions for the summit. Peace and development are likely to be key topics, Gao said. With global growth weak and industrial and supply chains under pressure, the three countries could explore cooperation to advance openness and development and give fresh impetus to the world economy. Zhang Tengjun, an associate research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of American Studies, said trilateral dialogue offers value that bilateral talks alone could not provide. A third country's participation could encourage each side to look beyond bilateral gains and losses, reassess one another's interests and concerns, and clarify strategic expectations. The format also offers an opportunity to explore more stable relations among major countries beyond bloc confrontation, Zhang said. Such dialogue would respond to widespread expectations that major powers should play a constructive role, a view held particularly among countries that want neither a return to Cold War-style divisions nor pressure to choose sides. Possible progress could include agreement in principle on addressing shared security challenges, support for political solutions to regional flashpoints, and greater clarity about each country's concerns and red lines, he said. Such exchanges could help establish a framework for managing relations and reduce the risk of strategic miscalculation. Zhang added that although the summit won't resolve all the challenges facing the international community overnight, holding it is nevertheless a positive and necessary step. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi urges further development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, highlighting the important mission of Guangdong province in effectively implementing the national strategy on promoting the region's integrated development. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks on Monday during an inspection tour of Zhongshan, Guangdong province. The trip was Xi's first domestic inspection tour after the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, a key Party meeting, was held in late October. He underlined the need to fully and faithfully implement the decisions and plans made at the session and better promote the integrated development of the east and west banks of the Pearl River Estuary. Xi inspected the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a mega cross-sea passage in South China that features two bridges, two artificial islands and an underwater tunnel. Spanning 24 kilometers, the link connects Zhongshan and the technology hub of Shenzhen — which lie on opposite sides of the Pearl River Estuary — slashing travel time from around two hours to about 30 minutes. At the west artificial island of the link, Xi learned about the construction and operation of the large-scale transportation project in the Greater Bay Area, another such project following the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, which is approximately 31 km south of the link. He said that to develop the Greater Bay Area, the first priority is to promote transportation integration. Noting that the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link has played a pioneering role in promoting the integrated development of the east and west banks of the Pearl River Estuary, he emphasized the importance of managing and operating this project well to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. The Greater Bay Area, which encompasses the Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions and nine cities in Guangdong, covers 56,000 square km. It achieved a total economic output of over 15 trillion yuan ($2.25 trillion) in 2025. China aims to develop the area into a world-class city cluster, a global technology and innovation center and a livable business-friendly location. While visiting the Future Technology Center of the Bay Area in Zhongshan's Cuiheng new district, Xi observed the development achievements of the city in modern industries such as biomedicine, electronic information and high-end equipment, as well as the display of traditional industrial products such as furniture. He learned about local efforts in undertaking industrial transfers, promoting the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries and developing emerging industries, while inquiring about the performance and market prospects of innovative products. Xi emphasized that building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan of the CPC Central Committee. Guangdong shoulders an important mission, and cities on both sides of the Pearl River Estuary, including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan, should play a leading role, he said. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan will seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a favorable business environment, and make great efforts to promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation for new progress in high-quality development. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. During the inspection tour, Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen in Cuiheng village, where Sun was born. He said that Sun made immortal contributions to national independence, social progress and people's well-being. He called for emulating, inheriting and carrying forward Sun's legacy to inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and realize national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization.

item.title: A link to APEC: Why are global youth choosing Hangzhou?
item.description:

As the world looks to the Asia-Pacific during APEC "China Year", we turn our lens to Hangzhou. item.title: Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Carney is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Canada to further advance their new strategic partnership, he added. Xi said China and Canada should build on the current momentum to enhance political mutual trust and steadily build the right perception of each other's development path and policy intent, deepen understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and settle differences and disagreements. The two countries should better align efforts to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade, energy, agriculture and finance, and expand cooperation in emerging areas including the green economy, e-commerce and the digital economy, in order to better harness each other's strengths and achieve win-win outcomes, he said. He called for deeper people-to-people exchanges and more exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, tourism, science, technology and youth as well as at subnational levels. He also proposed closer coordination to jointly practice true multilateralism, uphold the authority of the United Nations and the multilateral trading system, and build a more just and equitable global governance system. Carney said that bilateral relations have been on the right track of development since the launch of the Canada-China new strategic partnership during his meeting with Xi early this year. The two countries can fully advance and deepen cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, Carney said. Canada will work with China to pursue stronger cooperation in trade, investment, new energy, agricultural products, artificial intelligence, tourism and other areas, reduce the list of irritants, and expand the list of cooperation, he said. Canada stands ready to strengthen coordination with China to advance cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, uphold multilateralism, promote free trade, and contribute to stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region and the world, Carney added.

item.title: Xi meets Mexican president in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that advancing China-Mexico relations to new heights, across broader areas and in greater depth is of great significance to implementing their respective national development strategies and supporting the Global South in seeking strength through unity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. China is ready to work with Mexico to steer bilateral relations toward high-quality development, promote the building of an Asia Pacific that is prosperous, stable, open, interconnected, universally beneficial, inclusive, united and mutually supportive, as well as a more just and equitable global governance system, and contribute to world peace and common development, Xi added.

item.title: Xi says China ready to further develop ties with Peru
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Tuesday said China is ready to work with Peru to elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. China has remained Peru's largest trading partner and largest export destination country for 12 consecutive years, Xi said while meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Fujimori is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. Xi also noted that the protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement took effect officially about two weeks ago, and the Chancay Port, built with the participation of Chinese enterprises, has given a strong boost to economic and trade cooperation between Asia and Latin America.

item.title: Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that he is ready to work with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast to strengthen strategic guidance, keep to the right direction, and jointly draw a blueprint for the growth of bilateral relations, so as to support the development and prosperity of the two countries. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with Kast in Shenzhen. The Chilean president is in the southern Chinese city to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. The most valuable experience is that the two sides respect each other, treat each other as equals, and pursue win-win outcomes, he said. As this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Chile comprehensive strategic partnership and the 20th anniversary of the entry into force of the China-Chile Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral relations have reached an important juncture for building on past achievements and forging ahead into the future, Xi said.
